subject: Proposal: one-time make-good for Q1 burst and revised statement
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@tidesys.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@tidesys.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected Q1 inference spike — request for one-time adjustment

Hi Stephanie,

Hope you're well. We noticed a large, short-lived burst in our Q1 inference consumption (roughly 4x our committed baseline over a 48-hour window) that we believe was triggered by a batch import job that misfired from our side. We already patched the job, but the bill for that period pushed us well above our committed threshold.

Given TideSys is mid-renewal and evaluating a modest capacity bump for Q3, can Redwood consider a one-time make-good credit or an invoice adjustment for the anomalous hours? We prioritise long-term partnerships and want to resolve this cleanly — happy to share logs and a short summary of the root cause.

Attached: TideSys_Q1-usage-2027.csv (summary of daily inference hours and request IDs).

Thanks — can you confirm next steps? Our procurement lead is cc'd.

Best,
Olivia Park
Head of Cloud Ops, TideSys
olivia.park@tidesys.com
+1 415-555-0193
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@tidesys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, procurement@tidesys.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected Q1 inference spike — request for one-time adjustment

Hi Olivia — thanks for the data and context.

Quick read: that 48-hr window is clearly an outlier vs your 90-day median. We can do a one-time recon and propose a make-good credit for the portion of usage that exceeds your committed baseline, provided we can agree on the calculation and a PO or acceptance from procurement to finalize the billing change.

Proposed next steps:
- Ben will draft a transparent calculation showing how we isolate the burst usage (baseline vs spike) and the resulting credit amount.
- TideSys to confirm the root-cause summary and whether any downstream jobs remain scheduled (we want to ensure it's fully remediated).
- If accepted, we'll issue an adjusted invoice and apply the credit to your next renewal payment.

Looping in Ben and Lauren to own the reconciliation and invoicing. Ben — can you take the lead on the calculation and share a short spreadsheet by Friday? Lauren — can you advise on the invoicing/PO flow once we have agreement?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@tidesys.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, procurement@tidesys.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected Q1 inference spike — request for one-time adjustment

Hi all — attached is a draft calc (sng-proposed-makegood-calculation-20270423.xlsx). Summary below:

1) Baseline: TideSys committed 350 inference-hours/day (30-day lookback median used).
2) Q1 burst window (2027-03-04 00:00 UTC to 2027-03-06 23:59 UTC): average 1,420 inference-hours/day.
3) Billable excess = (burst average - baseline) * days in window = (1,420 - 350) * 3 = 3,210 excess hours.
4) Apply contracted overage rate of $0.045/hour = $144.45 gross.
5) Proposed one-time customer credit = 50% of gross overage = $72.23 credit applied as an invoice adjustment.

Rationale: we rarely offer full waivers for post-facto spikes; 50% is a compromise recognizing the customer is in active renewal and we want to preserve unit economics. If TideSys prefers a different split, we can accommodate but need procurement approval.

Requesting: TideSys procurement to confirm acceptance of the calculation and provide a PO number for the invoice change or sign the DocuSign link we will send.

Attachment: sng-proposed-makegood-calculation-20270423.xlsx (breakdown by day, request-id rollup, formula cells).

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@tidesys.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@tidesys.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Q1 inference spike — request for one-time adjustment

Thanks, Ben — appreciate the clear math. Procurement reviewed the calc and TideSys accepts the 50% credit as proposed. They asked that Redwood generate an adjusted invoice and a short acceptance doc so procurement can apply the credit on their side.

Please send an adjusted invoice referencing PO TS-4521 and a short DocuSign acceptance. Once we see the adjusted invoice, we will sign and release payment on the remaining balance.

Note: we confirmed the root cause (internal ETL misconfig) is fixed and there are no scheduled bulk jobs remaining.

Olivia

Subject: Final: adjusted invoice & credit applied (HS-7249)

Hi Olivia (and team),

Thanks for the confirmation and PO TS-4521. Per the agreed calculation, we've issued an adjusted invoice reflecting a $72.23 credit against the Q1 charge.

What we did:
- Generated adjusted invoice: adjusted-invoice-HS-7249-20270425.pdf (attached).
- Created short acceptance doc and routed via DocuSign (link sent separately to procurement@tidesys.com).
- Applied the credit as a line item and included the original usage breakdown for audit.

Expect the DocuSign to hit procurement shortly; once signed we'll mark the account as reconciled and reflect the adjustment in your next renewal statement.

If you want the credit applied immediately to the renewal payment instead of the Q1 invoice, reply with confirmation and we'll re-route.

Appreciate the quick turnaround from TideSys — happy to help as you scale capacity in Q3.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Billing Operations | Redwood Inference
